summary: Jacques P. Leider is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales. He served as director at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2001.

Jacques Scheuer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, the latter under Madeleine Biardeau, and held posts at Facultés Loyola Paris and Université catholique de Louvain.

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian who studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta from around 1887 to 1892. He later held a post at the University of Calcutta around 1926 to 1928.
Jae-seong Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1995, where he studied under Yasunori Ejima.

Jagdish Kashyap was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Kelaniya, and served as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from around 1951 to 1973.

Jake H. Davis works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, holding degrees from Marlboro College, the University of Hawaii, and CUNY Graduate Center. He taught at City College of New York, Brown University, and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the Basel Mission, Oxford, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held posts at the University of Marburg and the University of Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who earned degrees from Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA. He held academic posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

James A. Matisoff is a linguist who studied at Harvard University (~1954–1958) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1963–1967). He served on the faculty at UC Berkeley from around 1969 to 2008.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He has held positions as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).
James Atkinson was an Indologist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh. In 1818, he served as Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College.

James B. Apple specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed graduate studies and his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where his teachers included Geshe Lhundub Sopa and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

James Blumenthal was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who earned his PhD under Geshe Lhundub Sopa at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He later taught at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who founded The Indian Antiquary and Epigraphia Indica. He succeeded Alexander Cunningham in 1885 and served multiple times as head of the Archaeological Survey of India.

James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Richard Hugh Robinson, later becoming Associate Professor at the University of Northern Iowa.

James C. Dobbins is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies who completed his PhD at Yale University in 1984. He served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College.

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indology scholar who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He later served as professor of law at Presidency University, Kolkata.

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1964 to 1968 under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa around 1971.
James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Gibbs was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai from 1870 to 1879 and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from around 1876 to 1881.
